name: Sepu Vadi
subtitle: fried urad dal dumplings soaked soft in a spinach and yogurt gravy, the dish that marks a proper kangra dham

ingredients.note: thickens the gravy and holds the yogurt together
use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Soak the urad dal 5 hours. Drain it thoroughly - wet dal grinds into a batter that will not hold a shape.
Grind the dal with as little water as possible, then beat it by hand for 4 to 5 minutes until a spoonful floats in a glass of water. This aeration is what makes the vadis light.
Bring the yogurt to room temperature and whisk it with the besan so the gravy will not split.

steps.text: Grind the drained urad dal to a thick, coarse paste with the green chillies and grated ginger, using no more than 3 tbsp water.
steps.tip: Coarse, not silky. Sepu vadi should have a little bite left in it.

steps.text: Beat the paste vigorously for 4 to 5 minutes with salt until it lightens in colour and passes the float test.
Heat the frying oil to 170C. Drop in flat spoonfuls of the batter, four or five at a time, and fry 4 to 5 minutes until deep gold and firm. Drain on paper.
steps.tip: Too hot and the outside browns while the inside stays raw batter. A dropped bit should rise steadily, not violently.

steps.text: Cut each fried vadi in half through its thickness. This is what lets it drink up the gravy.
Boil the spinach in 200ml water for 4 minutes, then blend it to a smooth green puree with its liquid.
Heat the ghee in a kadhai, crackle the cumin, add the asafoetida and take the pan off the heat for a minute to cool.
On the lowest flame pour in the yogurt-besan mixture and stir continuously for 8 minutes until it thickens and stops smelling raw.
steps.tip: One direction, no stopping, low heat. If it splits there is no fixing it.

steps.text: Stir in the coriander powder, turmeric, kashmiri chilli, fennel and dry ginger, then the spinach puree and 200ml water. Season and simmer 8 minutes.
Slide in the halved vadis, cover and simmer very gently 10 minutes until they swell and turn spongy but still hold together.
steps.tip: Stir as little as possible now - a soaked vadi falls apart if you push it around.

steps.text: Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves and rest 5 minutes before serving with rice.

storage: Best the day it is made, while the vadis still have some structure. Keeps 2 days refrigerated; reheat covered on the lowest flame with a little water, without stirring.
